items.title: A transfer pricing model configured once and a rule-based generator turn documentation from an annual project into a button press
items.summary: Reptune.net is a rule-based generator: company types, functional analyses, transfer pricing methods and benchmarks are configured once in the model and Master File and Local Files are generated from it for groups of 5 to 500+ legal entities. Reptune states 50–75% time and cost savings versus traditional documentation, that clients are up and running in days without installation, and that the platform is trusted by 150+ multinationals, including TomTom, Stahl, Avnet, Ravago and Stanley Black & Decker. The generator ships OECD-aligned templates, localised templates (for example Italy), built-in validation and Excel bulk entry.
items.implication: The model — not the document — is the product: invest in model set-up (R-AI onboarding, bulk entry, validation) and in keeping generated output consistent across entities, because every hour saved in model configuration multiplies across all local files and every inconsistency is replicated everywhere.

items.title: BEPS Action 13's three-tiered documentation across 170+ countries makes country rule content the platform's hardest asset to copy
items.summary: OECD BEPS Action 13 introduced a three-tiered standardised approach to transfer pricing documentation: a Master File with group-wide information, a Local File per jurisdiction with the local entity's material transactions, and a Country-by-Country Report for large multinational groups, adopted by jurisdictions with local thresholds, content rules, languages and deadlines. Reptune states it automates documentation for 170+ countries (Vortex: 169+) with country-specific regulations, localised templates and local forms and procedures maintained in the platform.
items.implication: Treat the country regulation base — thresholds, content, format, language and deadline rules — as a first-class product with its own team, update lead time and currency metrics, and surface it both in the generator and in R-AI's country-expert answers; advisers and in-house teams pay for the countries they cannot cover themselves.

items.title: Auto-calculated deadlines, scoping, reminders and a worldmap dashboard turn documentation into a managed compliance process
items.summary: Reptune's workflow module scopes the documentation per entity and country, assigns tasks, sends e-mail reminders and auto-calculates deadlines for the Master File, Local Files, CbCR and CbCR notifications; the dashboard shows compliance status on a worldmap with filing deadlines per entity. The workflow is included in every plan, including Core, alongside unlimited users.
items.implication: The head of tax buys visibility as much as documents: make the dashboard the daily surface for group-wide status, drive the local contacts through assigned tasks rather than e-mail chains, and let deadline calculation depend on the country regulation base so that a rule change reprices every entity's deadline.

items.title: Public CbCR in XHTML with inline XBRL adds a second, machine-readable filing on top of the OECD XML report
items.summary: Directive (EU) 2021/2101 requires multinational groups with consolidated revenue above EUR 750 million to publish a country-by-country income tax report, in addition to the confidential OECD CbCR exchanged between tax authorities. Reptune produces CbCR in OECD XML and Excel, generates the EU Public CbCR in XHTML with inline XBRL, and announces Australian Public CbCR as coming; CbCR (OECD and EU public) is an add-on in the Core and Advanced plans and included in Enterprise.
items.implication: Model CbCR as one dataset with several renderings — OECD XML, Excel, EU public XHTML/inline XBRL, Australian public — so a new jurisdictional format is a renderer, not a new data collection; keep notification deadlines in the same engine as the reports.

items.title: Pillar Two's transitional CbCR safe harbour turns CbCR data quality into a tax-liability question, at a compliance cost the Tax Foundation puts in the billions for EU groups
items.summary: Under the Pillar Two transitional CbCR safe harbour, groups can rely on a qualified Country-by-Country Report and qualified financial statements to pass simplified de minimis, effective-tax-rate and routine-profits tests per jurisdiction, and so avoid full GloBE calculations there for the transition years. The Tax Foundation study of October 2025 (with ZEW) estimates one-off Pillar Two compliance costs for EU-headquartered groups at EUR 1.2 billion (up to EUR 2.0 billion) and recurring costs at EUR 517 million (up to EUR 865 million) per year, based on surveys of CFOs and heads of tax.
items.implication: Position CbCR data management as the entry point to Pillar Two readiness: validate CbCR datasets against entity financials and segmented P&Ls, keep an audit trail of the qualified data, and offer CbCR analysis as an advisory service; the head of tax will fund data quality when it changes a top-up tax outcome.

items.title: Three service levels on one platform let Reptune's specialists deliver at a fixed rate per Local File in a quarter of adviser time
items.summary: Reptune offers the platform with three service levels — On Demand (client-led), Collaborative (joint) and Full Service (Reptune-led) — at fixed rates per Local File, and states its specialists prepare documentation in 25% of the time a traditional adviser needs. Each plan includes expert hours (2, 4 or 8 per year) for on-demand advice, and the same workflow lets the client monitor progress while Reptune does the work. Reference testimonials cite Reptune having 'saved the day in various tax audits' and support on CbCR and value chain analysis.
items.implication: Build the full-service delivery workspace on the same bricks the client uses, so switching between service levels is a change of task assignment rather than a migration; measure specialist throughput per local file and rework, since margin at fixed rates depends on it.

items.title: The Legal Module ties time-stamped entity data and signed intercompany agreements to the documentation that cites them
items.summary: Reptune's Legal Module keeps time-stamped legal entity data, shareholders, directors and authorised signatories, an intercompany agreement repository, a corporate document repository, current and historical legal structure charts, and DocuSign integration for signing. Intercompany agreements and entity data feed the Master File and Local Files generated from the same platform.
items.implication: Make the legal counsel a first-class user rather than a data source: agreement coverage per intercompany transaction, entity data accuracy and signature turnaround become measurable, and an audit question about who signed what and when is answered from the repository instead of a mailbox.

items.title: Machine translation into 28 languages with glossaries and a human-certified option makes local language the last mile, not a separate project
items.summary: Reptune offers machine translation of generated documentation into 28 languages with client glossaries and a human-certified translation option, alongside localised templates and country-specific content rules, local forms and procedures. Machine translation is an add-on in the Core plan and included from Advanced upwards.
items.implication: Keep translation downstream of a single English source so a model change regenerates every language consistently; glossaries and country templates are content assets to maintain with the regulation base, and certified translation is a service line, not a feature.

items.title: R-AI and AI-assisted writing move onboarding and country expertise into the product, under ISO 27001 controls
items.summary: Reptune's R-AI assistant answers questions in any language, supports onboarding (included in every plan) and is offered as a Country Expert add-on, with a Local Requirements capability announced as coming; AI-assisted writing and editing is included in all plans. Reptune is ISO 27001 certified and offers a free two-week trial with no installation.
items.implication: Ground the assistant in the same regulation base and templates the generator uses, so an answer and a generated document never disagree; ISO 27001 and data handling are part of the evaluation for every head of tax, so AI features must be scoped to the client's own data and logged.

items.title: Operational transfer pricing — P&L segmentation, ERP integration and Excel mass upload — attacks the data collection bottleneck
items.summary: Reptune's operational transfer pricing offering covers P&L segmentation per entity and transaction, direct ERP integration and Excel mass upload, and compares segmented financials against benchmark ranges; the Enterprise plan adds a custom transactional data model and custom development. Data exchange and validation are included in every plan.
items.implication: Local finance provides most of the raw data, so validation at upload, a stable Excel interface and ERP connectors reduce the cycle time and error rate that decide whether local files are ready before the deadline; segmented results versus arm's-length ranges are the early warning for adjustments.

items.title: Vortex's 2024 majority stake funds commercial scaling and international expansion of a 20-person software-and-services company
items.summary: On 5 August 2024 Reptune (formerly TP Tuned, Amsterdam, founded 2015) announced that Vortex Capital Partners became majority shareholder alongside management; the company had 20 team members at the transaction. Lennart van den Kommer cited a 'proven offering and a loyal customer base' and the aim to 'serve more clients in additional countries and expand our offering'; Vortex's Evert Jan de Groot highlighted the proprietary software combined with deep transfer pricing knowledge. Vortex's stated focus is organisational infrastructure, commercial scaling, go-to-market, international expansion and possibly acquisitions.
items.implication: Growth beyond the founder-led base needs channels that scale without Reptune specialists on every file: adviser firms licensing the platform for many clients and in-house teams on On Demand plans; keep the services margin as proof of the product's leverage rather than the main revenue line.

items.title: Plans priced by local file count with unlimited users make the platform an adviser's leverage tool and an in-house team's budget line
items.summary: Reptune's Core plan covers up to 25 local files with unlimited users, the Automated Report Generator, dashboard, workflow, AI-assisted writing, R-AI onboarding, country regulations, report styling, data exchange and validation and 2 expert hours per year; Advanced covers up to 50 local files and adds SSO, R-AI Country Expert, custom text and 4 hours; Enterprise covers 50+ with custom user profiles, CbCR, divisions and 8 hours, with custom development as an add-on. Tax advisory firms license the platform to prepare documentation for several client groups.
items.implication: Divisions and client organisations must isolate client data for advisers while local-file counting stays the commercial unit; the upgrade path (SSO, custom templates, CbCR, divisions) should follow the natural growth of a group's entity count so expansion revenue comes without a re-sale.
